column1: # Tier 3 — Judged synthesis eval set (~25 questions)
# Columns: question<TAB>reference_answer
# - reference_answer is a single-line synthesis the judge treats as a
#   quality target. Multi-sentence answers stay on one line; use "\n"
#   literals (two-char) only if paragraph breaks are essential to the
#   comparison. The loader does NOT un-escape them.
# - Scoring is a 5-point rubric (faithfulness, coverage, calibration,
#   citation, conciseness) averaged. Pass threshold is 3.5.
# - These are open questions. Expect the judge, not exact-match. Tight
#   reference_answers bias the judge toward their style — keep them
#   information-dense but not prescriptive about phrasing.
question
column2: reference_answer

column1: What are the most common reported failure modes for L2 ADAS disengagements involving emergency braking on highways in 2025?
column2: Three themes dominate 2025 L2-ADAS highway complaints: (a) unprompted emergency braking triggered by overhead structures or shadows (~40% of cited narratives); (b) disengagement with no driver alert during lane changes near large trucks; (c) false target acquisition at on-ramp merges. Tesla, Ford, and GM account for most citations; remedies to date are OTA firmware updates. Cite at least one ODI ID per theme.

column1: Compare consumer complaints about transmission shifting between Honda and Toyota in MY 2022-2024.
column2: Honda complaints cluster around CVT hesitation and jerky downshifts in Civic/Accord 2022-2023, while Toyota complaints center on 8-speed automatic harsh 1-2 shifts in RAV4 Hybrid 2022-2024. Both OEMs issued TSBs (Honda 10-speed CVT software update; Toyota transmission strategy reflash). Volume is comparable; Toyota's complaints skew toward cold-start behaviour, Honda's toward highway merging.

column1: What are the recurring themes in Ford F-150 Lightning complaints since launch?
column2: Lightning complaints since 2022 cluster on: (1) charging faults at DC fast chargers, (2) 12V auxiliary battery failures causing bricking, (3) infotainment freezing/resets, (4) propulsion-loss events without warning, and (5) frunk latch issues. Ford has addressed several via TSB and OTA; TSB 10215120 targets the 12V issue. Citation-heavy answer expected.

column1: Summarise the trajectory of NHTSA investigations into Tesla Autopilot since 2021.
column2: 2021: PE21-020 opened on first-responder scene crashes. 2022: expanded to EA22-002 covering wider Autopilot scope. 2023: recall 23V-838 issued for Autopilot engagement-controls software update. 2024-2025: ongoing agency review of remedy sufficiency via EA24-XXX. Cite investigation and recall IDs; flag remaining uncertainty on recidivism data.

column1: What defects are most cited in Hyundai/Kia theft-related complaints 2020-2024?
column2: Recurring themes: vulnerability of mechanical ignitions to 'Kia challenge' social media attack; stolen vehicles recovered with ignition cylinders damaged; subsequent OEM software update + free steering lock campaign. Reference recall campaign(s) and multiple complaint IDs; flag overlap with insurance/legal response rather than technical defect.

column1: How have recall volumes for EV battery packs evolved 2022-2025?
column2: Steady rise driven by Hyundai-Kona, Chevy Bolt, Ford Mustang Mach-E packs in 2022-2023; shift in 2024 toward smaller-batch early-production EV truck recalls (Silverado EV, Lightning, Cybertruck). Median pack-replacement remedy time has decreased due to OTA diagnostic gating. Quantify with campaign counts and affected-vehicle totals.

column1: Describe the common complaint patterns for ADAS lane-keep assist nuisance activations across OEMs.
column2: Three patterns: (a) false activations in construction zones with repainted lines, (b) oversteer on exit ramps where lane markings diverge, (c) ping-pong between lanes on crowned rural roads. Complaints span Honda, Toyota, Subaru, GM. Remedies are typically calibration-only TSBs, not recalls. Expect 2-3 OEM examples and cite ODI ids.

column1: What is the pattern of SGO AV-crash reports by operator type 2023-2025?
column2: Waymo and Cruise dominate AV-mode reports through 2024; Cruise paused operations October 2023 reduced their share. Zoox and emerging operators (Aurora, Gatik) appear in 2025. Low-severity rear-end contact at intersections is the modal incident. Quantify where possible; cite SGO record IDs.

column1: What remedies have OEMs adopted for takata-adjacent inflator recalls after the initial campaigns?
column2: OEMs have moved from replace-with-like to replace-with-alternative-chemistry inflators; several extended-warranty programs for completion-rate uplift; multiple fragmentation recalls issued in 2023-2024 expanding affected populations. Cite 2-3 campaigns and flag still-outstanding completion gaps.

column1: Compare the quality picture for Rivian R1T/R1S and Lucid Air based on complaint volumes and themes 2023-2025.
column2: Rivian themes skew propulsion (stalling, charging), high-voltage; Lucid themes skew quality (panel fit, infotainment reset). Both OEMs show TSB-heavy remedy profiles, limited recall volumes vs. ICE peers. Volumes remain low in absolute terms due to smaller fleets. Cite representative ODI IDs.

column1: Describe how NHTSA investigations into Hyundai/Kia seat belt pretensioners evolved.
column2: Began with PE in 2022 after cluster of explosive failures during minor impacts; progressed to EA in 2023 after expanded scope; resulted in multi-brand recall affecting both Hyundai and Kia models. OEM supplier quality audit disclosed in final recall summary. Cite PE, EA, and recall identifiers.

column1: What trends appear in 2024 Class 8 truck (CDL) component recalls?
column2: Three clusters: air brake valves, fifth-wheel locking mechanisms, ADAS lane-departure warning calibration. Affected OEs include PACCAR, Daimler Trucks NA, Volvo Trucks. Lower campaign volumes than LV but high severity. Cite campaign IDs for each cluster.

column1: What are the dominant themes in SGO reports tagged 'Level 2' ADAS 2024?
column2: Level-2 SGO reports in 2024 cluster on (a) rear-end collisions during highway slowdowns, (b) side-swipe during automated lane-change assist, (c) failure to yield at 4-way stops with camera occlusion. Tesla FSD-beta vehicles dominate the report count; cite specific report numbers.

column1: Summarise known infotainment-related defect patterns across Stellantis brands 2022-2024.
column2: Stellantis Uconnect complaints cluster on reboot loops, Bluetooth pairing failures, CarPlay handoff issues. Multiple TSBs issued; no full recall as of 2024. Affected nameplates span Ram, Jeep, Dodge. Cite representative TSB numbers and ODI IDs.

column1: What are the typical root-cause patterns in NHTSA investigations that close without a recall?
column2: Typical reasons: insufficient failure rate vs. peer benchmark, remedy already available via existing TSB, OEM voluntary service campaign deemed adequate. Cite 2-3 PE/EA closures with final decision summaries.

column1: How has the split between OTA and dealer-visit remedies trended 2022-2025?
column2: Clear shift: ~10% OTA in 2022 recalls to ~35% in 2025. EV OEMs (Tesla, Rivian, Lucid, Ford F-150 Lightning) drive most OTA remedies. Dealer-only remedies still dominate safety-critical mechanical recalls. Cite 3-4 exemplar campaigns per year.

column1: What complaint themes distinguish BEV vs PHEV in 2024?
column2: BEV themes: charging, range, propulsion loss, 12V battery bricking. PHEV themes: engine-mode transition harshness, battery-depleted behaviour, infotainment handling of dual powertrain state. Cite at least 2 ODI examples of each.

column1: Compare heavy truck brake recalls issued by PACCAR vs. Daimler Trucks NA 2020-2024.
column2: Both OEMs issued multiple brake-system campaigns over the period; PACCAR campaigns concentrate on air-dryer / air-supply issues, Daimler campaigns on EBS module firmware and ABS sensor wiring. Volumes comparable; Daimler has higher remedy completion rate. Cite campaign numbers.

column1: What are the most common defects reported for electric motorcycles and scooters in 2024?
column2: Limited dataset, but themes: battery-pack fire during charging (multiple small-OEM campaigns), throttle-stuck-open complaints, regenerative brake grab. Cite the 2-3 campaigns present. Flag dataset-size caveat.

column1: Describe TSB patterns for over-the-air update rollbacks across OEMs.
column2: Fast-growing bulletin category; most TSBs published within 30 days of a flawed OTA release instruct dealers to roll back via USB flash or diagnostic-tool-forced downgrade. Tesla, Ford, GM, Stellantis all feature. Cite 2-3 TSB numbers and flag dataset sparsity in recent months.

column1: What defect patterns appear in school-bus recalls since 2020?
column2: Cluster of campaigns on (a) exhaust leak into cabin, (b) emergency-exit door latching, (c) brake master cylinder leaks, (d) electrical short near fuel filler. Low volume but high child-safety severity. Cite at least 3 campaigns with remedies.

column1: What are the recurring defect themes in Class 8 aftermarket DEF-system issues reported to NHTSA?
column2: Recurring themes: DEF pump heater element failure in cold climates, quality-control issues with the DEF quality sensor, NOx sensor faults triggering derate cycles. Primarily TSBs, few full recalls. Cite examples and flag overlap with EPA emission concerns.

column1: What quality signals does the ODI data show for new OEM entrants (Lucid, Rivian, Fisker, VinFast) 2023-2025?
column2: Rivian: steady complaint rate with propulsion + 12V themes. Lucid: low volume, fit/finish dominant. Fisker: complaints spike after company distress in 2024, many warranty-support issues. VinFast: low volume, infotainment and range accuracy issues. Cite representative IDs.

column1: What role have OTA 'phantom braking' fixes played in Tesla recalls 2022-2025?
column2: Multiple OTA-driven updates since 2022; two formal recalls (software-only remedy) in 2023 and 2024. Agency remains in ongoing review via EA. Cite the two recall campaign numbers and the open investigation.

column1: Summarise the current state of NHTSA engagement with rear cross-traffic alert defects.
column2: Growing cluster of complaints and a handful of TSBs; no standalone recall yet but several bundled under broader ADAS calibration campaigns. Affected OEMs span Nissan, Honda, Mazda. Cite TSBs and ODI IDs; flag that pattern is still pre-investigation.
